cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Hyoid bone

cards.question: Articulations
cards.answer: Does not articulate directly with any other bone; suspended by muscles and ligaments.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides attachment for tongue, suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles and helps support the larynx.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Body of hyoid bone
cards.label: 1a

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Central anterior part of the hyoid between the greater horns.
cards.label: 1a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Greater horn (cornu) of hyoid bone
cards.label: 1b

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Projects posterolaterally and provides muscular and ligamentous attachment.
cards.label: 1b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lesser horn (cornu) of hyoid bone
cards.label: 1c

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Gives attachment to the stylohyoid ligament.
cards.label: 1c

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Thyroid cartilage

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Largest laryngeal cartilage, formed by two laminae meeting anteriorly.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Protects the vocal apparatus and provides attachment for laryngeal muscles and ligaments.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Laryngeal prominence, superior and inferior horns, superior thyroid notch and oblique line.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior horn (cornu) of thyroid cartilage
cards.label: 2d

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Projects superiorly from the posterior border of the thyroid lamina toward the hyoid.
cards.label: 2d

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Inferior horn (cornu) of thyroid cartilage
cards.label: 2e

cards.question: Articulation
cards.answer: Articulates with cricoid cartilage at the cricothyroid joint.
cards.label: 2e

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cricoid cartilage

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Only complete cartilaginous ring of the airway; narrow anterior arch and broad posterior lamina.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Maintains airway patency and supports the arytenoid cartilages.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Inferior to thyroid cartilage and superior to the first tracheal ring.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Cricoid cartilage lies around C6, where the larynx continues as the trachea.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Arytenoid cartilage

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Paired pyramidal cartilages sitting on the superior border of the cricoid lamina.

cards.question: Landmarks
cards.answer: Each has a vocal process anteriorly and muscular process laterally.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Rotates and glides to abduct/adduct and tension the vocal folds.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Corniculate cartilage (cartilage of Santorini)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Small paired conical elastic cartilages atop the arytenoid cartilages.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lie within the aryepiglottic folds.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Support the posterior aryepiglottic folds.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cuneiform cartilage (cartilage of Wrisberg)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Small paired elastic cartilages embedded in the aryepiglottic folds.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Support and stiffen the aryepiglottic folds.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Tracheal cartilage

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings open posteriorly.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Maintain tracheal patency while permitting posterior oesophageal expansion.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Posterior gap is bridged by trachealis muscle and fibroelastic tissue.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Thyrohyoid membrane (median thyrohyoid ligament part)

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Spans between superior thyroid cartilage and hyoid; thickened centrally as the median thyrohyoid ligament.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Suspends the larynx from the hyoid bone.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Thyrohyoid membrane (lateral)

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Extends between thyroid cartilage and hyoid laterally.

cards.question: Contents
cards.answer: Pierced by the internal laryngeal nerve and superior laryngeal vessels.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Important landmark for the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Capsule of cricothyroid joint

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Fibrous capsule enclosing the synovial articulation between inferior horn of thyroid cartilage and cricoid cartilage.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Allows rotation and gliding that alter vocal-fold tension.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Median cricothyroid ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Connects inferior border of thyroid cartilage to superior border of cricoid arch in the midline.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Strengthens the anterior laryngeal framework.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Site used for emergency cricothyrotomy.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cricotracheal ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Connects inferior border of cricoid cartilage to the first tracheal ring.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Secures the larynx to the trachea while allowing movement.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Annular ligament of trachea

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Fibroelastic tissue connecting adjacent tracheal cartilage rings.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Provides flexibility while maintaining continuity of the tracheal wall.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Trachealis muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Narrows the tracheal lumen during coughing and relaxes to allow oesophageal expansion.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Autonomic fibres, mainly vagal parasympathetic with sympathetic input.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior ends of tracheal cartilage rings.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Spans the posterior membranous wall between the cartilage ends.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Thyrohyoid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Depresses the hyoid or elevates the larynx.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: C1 fibres travelling with the hypoglossal nerve.

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Oblique line of thyroid cartilage.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Inferior border of body and greater horn of hyoid.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Cricothyroid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Tenses and lengthens the vocal folds, increasing pitch.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: External branch of superior laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Anterolateral cricoid cartilage.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Inferior border and inferior horn of thyroid cartilage.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pars recta of cricothyroid muscle
cards.label: 16a

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: More vertical fibres contributing to thyroid-cricoid movement and vocal-fold tension.
cards.label: 16a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pars obliqua of cricothyroid muscle
cards.label: 16b

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Oblique fibres contributing to rotation/gliding at the cricothyroid joint and vocal-fold tension.
cards.label: 16b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Abducts the vocal folds by laterally rotating arytenoid cartilages and opens the rima glottidis.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior surface of cricoid lamina.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Muscular process of arytenoid cartilage.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Only muscle that abducts the vocal folds; bilateral paralysis can critically obstruct the airway.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Transverse arytenoid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts arytenoid cartilages and closes the posterior rima glottidis.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Posterior surface of one arytenoid cartilage.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Posterior surface of the opposite arytenoid cartilage.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Oblique arytenoid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts arytenoid cartilages and helps close the laryngeal inlet.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Muscular process of one arytenoid cartilage.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Apex of the opposite arytenoid; continues into aryepiglottic fibres.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Adducts the vocal folds by medially rotating the arytenoid cartilages.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Upper border of lateral cricoid arch.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Muscular process of arytenoid cartilage.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Aryepiglottic muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Narrows the laryngeal inlet by drawing the aryepiglottic folds together.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve via inferior laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of oblique arytenoid fibres.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral margin of epiglottis and aryepiglottic fold.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Thyroarytenoid muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Relaxes and shortens the vocal folds and assists adduction.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Inner surface of thyroid cartilage near the angle.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Anterolateral surface and vocal process of arytenoid cartilage.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Deep part of thyroarytenoid muscle
cards.label: 22a

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Medial fibres contribute to fine adjustment of vocal-fold tension and are closely related to vocalis.
cards.label: 22a

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: External part of thyroarytenoid muscle
cards.label: 22b

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Lateral fibres help shorten and relax the vocal folds and contribute to laryngeal closure.
cards.label: 22b

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Thyroepiglottic muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Widens the laryngeal inlet by drawing the epiglottis laterally.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve via inferior laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Continuation of thyroarytenoid fibres.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Lateral margin of epiglottis and aryepiglottic fold.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Stylopharyngeus muscle

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Elevates the pharynx and larynx during swallowing and speech.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Styloid process.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Pharyngeal wall and posterior border of thyroid cartilage.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vocalis muscle (medial part of thyroarytenoid muscle)

cards.question: Actions
cards.answer: Fine-tunes vocal-fold tension by selectively tensing or relaxing portions of the vocal ligament.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Inner thyroid angle/anterior vocal-ligament region.

cards.question: Insertion
cards.answer: Vocal process and adjacent arytenoid cartilage.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior thyroid artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually the first anterior branch of the external carotid artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends toward the superior pole of the thyroid gland.

cards.question: Branches
cards.answer: Gives the superior laryngeal artery among other branches.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Upper thyroid gland and nearby laryngeal and infrahyoid structures.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior laryngeal artery

cards.question: Origin
cards.answer: Usually a branch of the superior thyroid artery.

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Pierces the thyrohyoid membrane with the internal laryngeal nerve.

cards.question: Supply
cards.answer: Supplies the upper laryngeal mucosa and structures.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Superior laryngeal nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branch of the vagus nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Descends from the vagus and divides into internal and external branches near the hyoid/larynx.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: External branch supplies cricothyroid and contributes to inferior pharyngeal constrictor innervation.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Internal branch provides sensation above the vocal folds and forms an important afferent limb of the cough reflex.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: External branch injury causes reduced ability to produce high-pitched sounds and voice fatigue; internal branch injury reduces supraglottic sensation and the cough reflex, increasing aspiration risk.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Recurrent laryngeal nerve

cards.question: Roots
cards.answer: Branch of the vagus nerve (CN X).

cards.question: Course
cards.answer: Right loops under the subclavian artery; left loops under the aortic arch near the ligamentum arteriosum; both ascend in the tracheo-oesophageal groove and enter the larynx as inferior laryngeal nerves.

cards.question: Motor functions
cards.answer: Supplies all intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid.

cards.question: Sensory functions
cards.answer: Supplies laryngeal mucosa below the vocal folds.

cards.question: Lesion
cards.answer: Unilateral injury causes hoarseness from ipsilateral vocal-fold paralysis; bilateral injury can cause severe airway obstruction because both vocal folds may remain near the midline.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: At risk in thyroid surgery and mediastinal pathology; the left nerve may be affected by aortic arch enlargement.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Epiglottic cartilage

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Leaf-shaped elastic cartilage forming the structural core of the epiglottis.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Helps protect the laryngeal inlet during swallowing.

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Connected to thyroid cartilage by the thyroepiglottic ligament and to hyoid by the hyoepiglottic ligament.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Hyoepiglottic ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Connects the anterior surface of the epiglottis to the body of the hyoid.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Helps anchor the epiglottis to the hyoid.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Thyroepiglottic ligament

cards.question: Attachments
cards.answer: Connects the petiole of the epiglottis to the inner surface of the thyroid cartilage.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Anchors the epiglottis inferiorly within the laryngeal framework.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Ventricle of the larynx

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Recess between the vestibular fold superiorly and vocal fold inferiorly.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Permits independent movement of the folds and communicates with the laryngeal saccule.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vestibular fold (false vocal cord)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Mucosal fold containing the vestibular ligament.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Helps protect the airway and contributes to laryngeal closure.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: Lies superior to the true vocal fold.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Vocal fold (true vocal cord)

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Contains the vocal ligament and vocalis muscle, covered by mucosa.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Vibrates during phonation and closes the glottis for airway protection.

cards.question: Innervation
cards.answer: Motor control via recurrent laryngeal nerve except cricothyroid tensioning via external superior laryngeal nerve.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Impaired mobility causes dysphonia; bilateral dysfunction can threaten the airway.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Mucous membrane of the trachea

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Respiratory mucosa lined mainly by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Warms, humidifies and clears inhaled particles via the mucociliary escalator.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Epiglottic vallecula

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Depression between the base of the tongue and epiglottis.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Important landmark during direct laryngoscopy; the tip of a Macintosh blade is commonly placed here.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Piriform recess

cards.question: Location
cards.answer: Mucosal recess of the laryngopharynx lateral to the laryngeal inlet.

cards.question: Relations
cards.answer: The internal laryngeal nerve lies deep to the mucosa in this region.

cards.question: Clinical relevance
cards.answer: Foreign bodies may lodge here and can damage the internal laryngeal nerve.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Pharyngoepiglottic fold

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Mucosal fold extending from the lateral epiglottis toward the pharyngeal wall.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Contributes to the boundary of the laryngeal inlet and channels swallowed material laterally.

cards.question: Identification
cards.answer: Aryepiglottic fold

cards.question: Structure
cards.answer: Mucosal fold extending from arytenoid cartilage to lateral epiglottis and containing aryepiglottic muscle and small cartilages.

cards.question: Function
cards.answer: Forms the lateral margin of the laryngeal inlet and helps close it during swallowing.
